results.evidence: The exhibit explicitly labels the EMPhASIS data as 'Long-Term Phase 2 EMPhASIS Data' and separately identifies the Phase 3 ENSURE trials as the catalyst ('Top-Line Data from Twin Phase 3 ENSURE Trials... Expected by Year-End 2026'). The Phase 2 open-label source is disclosed in the headline itself, not masked, and is presented as supportive long-term safety/disability data distinct from the pivotal readout.

The exhibit explicitly labels the EMPhASIS data as 'phase 2' 'OLE period' (open-label extension) in the same sentence as the claim, and the surrounding text frames it as long-term safety/tolerability data (5.5 years, ~952 treatment-years, discontinuation rates, AE profile) — not as a substitute for the pending randomized phase 3 readout. The exhibit separately and clearly identifies the success-determining catalyst as 'top-line data from the twin phase 3 ENSURE-1 and ENSURE-2 trials in RMS... expected by the end of 2026.' The OLE is disclosed as what it is, not slotted into the pivotal-success position.

The exhibit explicitly labels the disability-worsening data as 'Long-Term Data From Phase 2 EMPhASIS Trial' — i.e., the phase 2 predecessor, not the phase 3 catalyst trials. The headline structure separates CALLIPER (progressive MS) and EMPhASIS (RRMS phase 2 long-term) data; nothing in the flagged sentence claims this is pivotal phase 3 efficacy, so describing supportive open-label extension data as such is disclosure, not masking of the phase 3 readout.
